title: 50 storey tower, Brisbane CBD: structure
note: Facts are example inputs for testing. On a real project they come from the project's own designs and procedures.

swms.title: Floor load-out, working with the tower cranes, and forklifts
swms.task: Load out each floor of the 50 storey tower using the two tower cranes and the loading platforms, and move materials on the floor with a forklift. Deliveries are unloaded from the street loading zone next to the road, open to traffic, with traffic controllers. The floors are post-tensioned slabs. Work is at the slab edge, more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.fallControl: Loading platforms have full height gates and side screens, and the slab edge has perimeter screens on every level being worked.
facts.systemInstructions: Loading platforms are the supplier's system, installed to its instructions LP-01 revision 3 by its trained installers.
facts.loadLimits: Load limits for each floor and the loading platforms are on the formwork engineer's load plan LP-10. They are signed at each landing area, and the formwork supervisor checks them before each load-out.

steps: Work with the crane crew during lifts
Separate plant and people on site

swms.title: Slab formwork, falsework, stripping and backpropping
swms.task: Erect the slab formwork and falsework for each post-tensioned floor of the 50 storey tower, lay the deck, form penetrations, install edge protection, then strip the formwork and install backprops. Materials are lifted with the tower cranes. Work is at the slab edge and up to 4 m above the floor below.

facts.formworkDesign: Formwork, falsework and backpropping designed by the formwork engineer, drawings FW-100 to FW-120. The formwork supervisor inspects and signs the pre-pour checklist before every pour.
facts.fallControl: Perimeter screens are installed on the levels being formed, decks are laid from inside the edge protection, and penetrations are covered as they are formed.
facts.systemInstructions: The deck system and props are the formwork supplier's proprietary system, erected to its assembly instructions FS-200 revision 5. The crew is trained by the supplier.
facts.loadLimits: The formwork deck is designed for the construction loads on drawing FW-101, including ply packs of no more than 1.5 t per landing area over the bearers. Limits are signed on the deck and checked by the formwork supervisor.

steps: Work with the crane crew during lifts
Load ply onto the deck while it is being laid

swms.title: Reo fixing and post-tensioning tendon placement
swms.task: Lift reo bundles onto the deck with the tower cranes, place and tie the reinforcement, and place the post-tensioning ducts and tendons for each floor slab of the 50 storey tower. Work is at the slab edge, more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.fallControl: Work is done inside the perimeter screens, and no one works outside the edge protection.
facts.loadLimits: Reo bundles are landed within the deck loads on the formwork engineer's drawing FW-101, spread over the bearers. The steel fixing supervisor checks each landing against the signed limits.

steps: Work with the crane crew during lifts

swms.title: Concrete pumping, placing and finishing
swms.task: Pump concrete with a concrete pump truck in the street loading zone and a placing boom on the slab, then place and finish the concrete for each post-tensioned floor slab of the 50 storey tower. Work is at the slab edge, more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.fallControl: Perimeter screens stay in place during the pour, and the deck is complete with penetrations covered before the pour starts.

steps: Set up the concrete pump and placing boom

swms.title: Post-tensioning stressing and grouting
swms.task: Stress the post-tensioning tendons on each floor slab of the 50 storey tower once the concrete reaches the engineer's strength, grout the ducts and cut the tendon tails. Stressing is done at the slab edge, more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.stressingProcedure: Stressing follows the post-tensioning engineer's sequence on drawing PT-200, once cylinder tests show the strength the engineer requires. The post-tensioning subcontractor's trained crew does the stressing. Exclusion zones behind each jack and along the tendon line are barricaded and signed.
facts.fallControl: Stressing is done from inside the perimeter screens, which stay in place until stressing is complete.

swms.title: Core jumpform climbing and core wall construction
swms.task: Climb the jumpform on the core walls of the 50 storey tower with its hydraulic climbing system, then fix reo and pour the core walls from the jumpform platforms, more than 2 m above the floor below. The tower cranes lift materials to the jumpform.

facts.jumpformProcedure: Climbing follows the jumpform supplier's climbing procedure JF-OPS revision 3, including its wind limit. Only the climbing crew trained and assessed by the supplier climbs the jumpform.
facts.fallControl: The jumpform platforms have full perimeter screens and guardrails, and the gaps to the wall are closed with hinged flaps.

steps: Work with the crane crew during lifts
Fix the wall reo from the platforms
Set the wall forms from the platforms

swms.title: Precast column and blade wall installation
swms.task: Install precast concrete columns and blade walls with the tower cranes, lifting them from trucks in the street loading zone, stand them on shims, brace them, then grout the base. The floors are post-tensioned slabs. Work is at the slab edge of the 50 storey tower, more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.erectionDesign: Precast erection design and sequence drawings PC-300 to PC-305 by the precast engineer.
facts.centreOfGravity: The centre of gravity is marked on each element's shop drawing.
facts.braceArrangement: Two braces per column and three per blade wall, fixed to the slab with cast-in ferrules as shown on drawing PC-310.
facts.fallControl: Work is done from inside the perimeter screens, and rigging at height is released from an elevating work platform.
facts.harnessSystem: Workers wear a full body harness with a restraint lanyard short enough that they cannot be thrown from the basket, clipped to the boom lift anchor point. Harnesses and lanyards are checked by the user before each use and inspected by a competent person every 6 months, recorded on the tag. Users are trained in working at heights and boom lift operation by a registered training organisation.

steps: Work with the crane crew during lifts
Stand and brace the precast elements
